title: Fox News Op-Ed Calls for Eliminating H-1B and OPT Programs, Citing Worker Replacement
excerpt: <pA Fox News opinion piece published this week has reignited the contentious debate over America's legal immigration system, specifically calling for the complete elimination of the H1B and Optional Practical Training…
body:
A Fox News opinion piece published this week has reignited the contentious debate over America's legal immigration system, specifically calling for the complete elimination of the H-1B and Optional Practical Training (OPT) programs — two pathways that hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals and students depend on annually.

The Core Argument: Legal Immigration as Worker Replacement

The op-ed argues that America's legal immigration framework has been "designed by corporate lobbyists" to enable corporations, particularly in the technology sector, to "quietly replace American workers with visa-sponsored immigrants." The piece characterizes the H-1B program as "a loosely monitored system that allows cheap and often entry-level workers to occupy jobs that Americans would gladly fill."

Supporting this claim, the article cites Department of Homeland Security data showing that 83% of H-1B visas petitioned between 2020 and 2024 were for entry and junior-level positions with salaries below the local median wage. The Department of Labor reportedly found that minimum wages for H-1B workers are set $19,000 lower than what American workers earn in equivalent roles.

OPT Program Under Fire

The Optional Practical Training program came under particularly sharp criticism. The op-ed notes that OPT has "no cap on the number of participants, no requirement that the employer at least try to hire Americans" before using the program, and "no legal minimum salary." Currently, more than 400,000 foreign students are working through OPT, predominantly in technology and engineering fields.

The piece also highlighted that OPT participants remain on student visas, which allows employers to avoid payroll taxes — creating what critics call an additional financial incentive to hire foreign workers over American candidates.

Fraud Allegations Compound the Debate

Adding fuel to the fire, the op-ed referenced President Trump's fraud task force, which reportedly identified more than 10,000 cases of foreign students in OPT claiming employment with "suspect or nonexistent employers." A separate Fox News report noted that authorities had uncovered networks of Indian universities allegedly selling counterfeit degrees used to obtain H-1B visas.

What This Means for the Indian Diaspora

Indian nationals are by far the largest beneficiary group of both the H-1B and OPT programs. Any legislative action to curtail or eliminate these programs would disproportionately affect Indian professionals already in the United States and those planning to come. The op-ed's call for ending both programs entirely — rather than reforming them — represents an extreme position, but it reflects a growing anti-immigration sentiment that has been gaining traction in certain political circles.

Meanwhile, the Center for Immigration Studies data cited in the piece — showing 11 million Americans with STEM degrees not working in STEM — has been contested by immigration advocates who argue that many of those individuals chose other career paths voluntarily and that the tech industry continues to face genuine talent shortages in specialized areas.

The debate comes at a time when USCIS has already confirmed that the H-1B cap for FY 2027 has been reached, leaving thousands of Indian professionals uncertain about their immigration future in the United States.
